//: WI-AF3.2 — a review deadline for every committed baseline, so frozen debt is
SCHEDULED rather than merely visible. Finding F5: ~450 units of debt were frozen
across 27 baselines and none had moved in the five days since they were measured.
A ratchet stops debt growing; it never asks anyone to pay it.
DATES ARE INTEGERS (YYYYMMDD) ON PURPOSE. Registered in the ratchet manifest as
`per-key-count` over `reviews`, so pushing a deadline OUT is numerically a raise
and fails against the merge base, while pulling one IN passes. That means the
authorized-exception path is `allowRaise` — the mechanism this repo already
trusts: one re-measurement, a mandatory reason, and it fails as stale once the
base carries the new value. An earlier draft of the plan invented a parallel
`deferReview` mechanism; it could not have worked, because the ratchet loads the
manifest from HEAD only and never at the base. Moving the dates into a JSON
baseline put them somewhere the existing machinery can already read historically.
OVERDUE DOES NOT BLOCK A PR. `scripts/check-review-schedule.mjs --report` runs on
a schedule and files a rolling issue. A calendar-triggered CI failure would redden
an unrelated PR with nothing its author can do, which is how a gate gets disabled.
The PR tier enforces only that this file is not quietly loosened.
KEYS are `<baseline path>` — one deadline per baseline, not per check. A file with
four checks (file-size) is one debt with one owner.
EXEMPT is a claim that a baseline is not debt, and requires a reason. Vendored
upstream corpora and inventories of what exists are not things anyone should be
asked to drive to zero. A stale exemption fails like any other stale allowlist:
every manifest entry must appear in exactly one of `reviews` or `exempt`, and
every key here must name a real manifest entry.

owners.//: One owner per dated baseline. `maintainer` is honest here — this is a solo repo, and inventing team names would make the field decorative.

targets.scripts/mock-boundaries-baseline.json: zero — tests use the real store (setState/reset) or a recorded store-factory seam
targets.scripts/command-error-baseline.json: zero — every command returns Result<T, CommandError>
targets..dependency-cruiser-known-violations.jso: down — each frozen edge either deleted or re-expressed through a plugins/shared seam
targets.scripts/plugin-store-coupling-baseline.j: zero on every channel — options and seams, not ambient lookups
targets.scripts/file-size-baseline.json: down — split files, lower the number; never raise
targets.scripts/knip-baseline.json: zero — delete the dead export or justify it at the definition
targets.scripts/bespoke-buttons-baseline.json: down — each bespoke class converted to .vm-btn / .popup-icon-btn
targets.scripts/extension-budget.json: down — per-edge licenses retired as plugins decouple
targets.scripts/merge-drop-allowlist.json: zero — every allowed drop either fixed or shown to be intended
targets.src/utils/markdownPipeline/__tests__/spe: down — each declared divergence fixed or ruled a deliberate dialect choice

exempt.scripts/shell-slots-baseline.json: An INVENTORY, not debt: the identity list of the surfaces App.tsx mounts. It should track reality, and reality has ~20 surfaces. Driving it to zero would mean an app with no UI.
exempt.scripts/i18n-untranslated-baseline.json: Already zero — the ~1,160-entry debt was paid. The gate exists to keep it there, so there is nothing to schedule.
exempt.scripts/i18nIdenticalAllowlist.ts: A permanent registry of genuinely untranslatable strings (runner labels, literal paths), each with a stated reason and checked for staleness in both directions. Not a number anyone should drive down.
exempt.src/utils/markdownPipeline/__tests__/spe: Vendored upstream conformance corpus — test DATA, not debt.
Vendored upstream corpus — XSS payloads that must keep being escaped.
Vendored corpus for the md→ProseMirror oracle.
exempt.scripts/baseline-review-schedule.json: The schedule itself. Its dates ratchet like any baseline, but a deadline for reviewing the deadlines is bureaucracy, not debt.
